v.why: Raising an already large learning rate pushes training toward divergence, as in runs 7 and 8, so the loss is larger than at small learning rates.
At very small learning rates the 243-epoch training budget leaves the network underfit, so a larger step helps (runs 1 and 2).
Reducing a too-large learning rate restores stable training, with large gains in runs 11, 12 and 20.
Lowering an already tiny learning rate worsens underfitting within the fixed number of epochs.
Shallower networks are more stable at a high learning rate, as runs 54 and 58 show.
Extra depth amplifies instability when the learning rate is large (runs 42 and 48).
Wider layers have larger effective update magnitudes at a high learning rate, which makes divergence more likely (run 66).
Smaller batches give noisier gradients, which hurts when the learning rate is already high (runs 34 and 36).
Strong L2 regularization underfits, so weakening it helps (runs 91, 92 and 100).
Pushing already strong L2 higher causes heavy underfitting (run 89).
